hook.text: Before 1982, diabetics injected pig or cow insulin — it sometimes caused allergic reactions. Then came Humulin.

buildup.text: Genentech inserted the human insulin gene into E. coli bacteria — the microbes became tiny insulin factories.

discovery.text: Humulin was the first recombinant drug approved by the FDA — identical to human insulin, made by bacteria.

twist.text: Modern insulin analogs are engineered beyond human — lispro acts faster, glargine lasts longer. Better than nature.

climax.text: Over 100 million people depend on recombinant insulin — the first biopharmaceutical saved an entire industry.

punchline.text: Bacteria make human insulin — biotech's first drug, still saving lives.

quiz.question: What made Humulin historically significant?
options: It was the first insulin that could be taken orally
It was the first recombinant DNA drug approved by the FDA
It was extracted from a new animal source

details.summary: Recombinant human insulin, produced in engineered bacteria or yeast, replaced animal-derived insulin that caused allergic reactions in some diabetic patients. First approved in 1982, it was the original recombinant biopharmaceutical and proved biotechnology could transform medicine.
details.whyItMatters: Recombinant insulin was biotechnology's proof of concept. It demonstrated that genetic engineering could produce human proteins at industrial scale, launching a multi-billion-dollar industry and ensuring reliable insulin supply for millions of
takeaways: Recombinant insulin was the first biotechnology drug approved in 1982
It replaced animal insulin that caused immune reactions in some patients
Engineered insulin analogs now provide rapid-acting and long-acting options

faq.question: How is recombinant insulin produced?
faq.answer: The human insulin gene is inserted into E. coli bacteria or yeast cells that produce the protein during fermentation. The insulin is then purified, properly folded, and processed. Modern production yields tons of pure human insulin annually from industrial-scale fermenters.

faq.question: What are insulin analogs and how do they differ from human insulin?
faq.answer: Insulin analogs have modified amino acid sequences that alter absorption speed. Rapid-acting analogs like lispro work in minutes for mealtime coverage. Long-acting analogs like glargine provide steady 24-hour basal coverage. These innovations improved blood sugar control and quality of life.
